outputs.L1: An image display system includes: acquisition means for acquiring operation information indicating a moving direction and a moving amount of an input position during an input operation performed on a first display object while the first display object is displayed on a display device; extraction means for, when the moving amount of the input position in a predetermined first direction exceeds a predetermined threshold, acquiring a first attribute parameter of the first display object corresponding to the first direction and extracting, from storage means in which a plurality of display objects are associated with attribute parameters, a second display object that is associated with the first display object and has a first attribute parameter different from that of the first display object; and display control means for displaying the second display object extracted by the extraction means on the display device in place of the first display object.
outputs.L2: An image display system comprises an acquisition unit, an extraction unit, and a display control unit. While a first display object is shown on a display device, the acquisition unit obtains operation data indicating the direction and distance of movement of an input position during an input operation performed on that object. If the input position moves in a specified first direction by more than a predefined threshold, the extraction unit obtains a first attribute parameter of the first display object corresponding to that direction. It then searches storage containing multiple display objects linked to attribute parameters and selects a second display object that is associated with the first display object but has a different first attribute parameter. The display control unit replaces the first display object on the display device with the selected second display object.
outputs.L3: The image display system acquires operation information indicating the direction and amount of movement of an input position on a first display object while that object is displayed on a display device. When the movement in a predetermined first direction exceeds a specified threshold, the system obtains an attribute parameter associated with the first display object. It then identifies and extracts a related second display object having a corresponding attribute parameter that differs from that of the first display object. The display control subsequently replaces the first display object with the extracted second display object on the display device.
outputs.L4:
An image display system provides gesture-based navigation among a collection of related display objects. The system includes a display unit, an input interface capable of detecting a user gesture, a storage or retrieval unit containing multiple display objects, and a controller that manages presentation of the objects. Each display object is associated with one or more attributes, such as time, position, category, sequence number, viewpoint, magnification level, or another characteristic by which related objects may be organized.

When a user performs a gesture on or in relation to a currently displayed object, the system detects the gesture and tracks both its direction and travel distance. The gesture may be entered through a touch-sensitive display, a pointing device, a motion sensor, or another suitable input mechanism. The controller compares the detected movement with a predetermined directional condition and distance threshold. Minor or unintended movement may therefore be ignored, while a deliberate movement that proceeds sufficiently far in a specified direction is treated as a navigation command.

In response to determining that the gesture satisfies the applicable conditions, the system identifies an attribute corresponding to the gesture direction. For example, movement to the right may request an object having a later sequence value, while movement to the left may request an object having an earlier sequence value. Upward or downward movement may similarly correspond to changes in another attribute, such as category, depth, viewpoint, or level of detail. The system then retrieves a related display object whose corresponding attribute differs from that of the currently displayed object in the manner indicated by the gesture.

After the related object has been retrieved, the controller replaces the original object with the retrieved object on the display. The replacement may occur immediately or may be accompanied by a transition animation that reflects the direction of the user’s gesture. In this way, users can move naturally among associated images, documents, icons, records, or other visual objects without relying on separate navigation buttons or complex menu operations. The use of directional and distance-based gesture evaluation also helps distinguish intentional navigation commands from incidental contact, providing an intuitive and reliable interface for browsing related content.

## An Image Display

An image display is a visual interface used to present photographs, illustrations, graphics, or digital artwork. It may take the form of a computer screen, digital frame, gallery wall, projector, or mobile device. A well-designed image display highlights details through appropriate brightness, color accuracy, resolution, and contrast. The arrangement of images also affects how viewers understand and experience the content. Whether used for education, entertainment, advertising, or personal memories, an effective image display makes visual information clear, engaging, and accessible.
